prompt:
Consider a regular polygon with $2^n$ sides, for $n\ge2$, inscribed in a circle of radius $1$. Denote the area of this polygon by $A_n$. Compute
$$\prod_{i=2}^{\infty}\frac{A_i}{A_{i+1}}.$$

solutions.title: Telescoping product
solutions.body:
The partial product telescopes: $\prod_{i=2}^{N}\frac{A_i}{A_{i+1}}=\frac{A_2}{A_{N+1}}$. Here $A_2$ is the area of the inscribed square, $2$, and $A_{N+1}\to\pi$ (the area of the circle) as $N\to\infty$. So the product is $\frac2\pi$.

**Answer: $\frac2\pi$**
